stem: A flowering room's timer is consistent, but staff occasionally perform maintenance under white light during the intended dark interval. Which corrective approach best protects the validity of the flowering schedule?
choices: Continue the maintenance practice when the timer log is normal because service-light exposure can be evaluated separately from the programmed photoperiod
Adjust daytime irrigation and airflow around maintenance events while leaving the dark-period lighting practice unchanged
Shorten the next scheduled light period by the maintenance duration to compensate for the earlier interruption of darkness
Eliminate or tightly control unintended dark-period illumination and verify the actual room light conditions during that interval
rationale: Photoperiod-sensitive flowering depends on the light-dark environment actually experienced by the plant. Operational controls should therefore protect the intended dark interval and verify real conditions rather than relying only on timer settings.
